cues.en: I'm gonna talk to you about some stuff that's in this book of mine that I hope will resonate with other things that you've already heard, and I'll try to make some connections myself in case you missed them. But I wanna start with what I call the official dogma.
cues.zh: 我要和你们谈谈我这本书里的一些内容，希望能和你们已经听过的其他东西产生共鸣，我也会尝试自己建立一些联系，以防你们错过了。但我想先从我所说的“官方教条”开始。

cues.en: The official dogma of what? The official dogma of all Western industrial societies.
cues.zh: 什么官方教条？所有西方工业社会的官方教条。

cues.en: And the official dogma runs like this. If we are interested in maximizing the welfare of our citizens,
cues.zh: 这个官方教条是这样的：如果我们想最大化公民的福祉，

cues.en: the way to do that
cues.zh: 实现这一点的途径

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 就是

cues.en: to maximize individual freedom.
cues.zh: 最大化个人自由。

cues.en: The reason for this is both that freedom is in and of itself good,
cues.zh: 原因是，自由本身就是好的、

cues.en: valuable,
cues.zh: 有价值的、

cues.en: worthwhile, essential to being human,
cues.zh: 值得追求的、作为人必不可少的，

cues.en: and because if people have freedom, then each of us can act on our own to do the things that will maximize our welfare, and no one has to decide on our behalf.
cues.zh: 而且，如果人们拥有自由，那么我们每个人都能自行采取行动，去做那些能最大化我们福祉的事，无需别人替我们做决定。

cues.en: The way to maximize freedom is to maximize choice.
cues.zh: 最大化自由的方式就是最大化选择。

cues.en: The more choice people have,
cues.zh: 人们拥有的选择越多，

cues.en: the more freedom they have. And the more freedom they have, the more welfare they have.
cues.zh: 他们拥有的自由就越多。而他们拥有的自由越多，他们拥有的福祉就越多。

cues.en: This, I think, is so
cues.zh: 我认为这一点已经

cues.en: deeply embedded in the water supply that it wouldn't occur to anyone to question it.
cues.zh: 深深嵌入我们的供水系统（思想环境）中，以至于没人会想到去质疑它。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: it's also deeply embedded in our lives.
cues.zh: 它也深深嵌入我们的生活中。

cues.en: I'll give you some examples
cues.zh: 我给你们举些例子，

cues.en: of what modern progress has made possible for us. This is my supermarket,
cues.zh: 说明现代进步为我们带来了什么。这是我的超市，

cues.en: not such a big one.
cues.zh: 不算太大。

cues.en: I wanna say just a word about salad dressing. A 175 salad dressings in my supermarket, if you don't count the 10 extra virgin olive oils and 12 balsamic vinegars you could buy to make a very large number of your own salad dressings in the off chance that none of the 175
cues.zh: 我想简单说一下沙拉酱。我的超市里有175种沙拉酱，这还不算你可以买到的10种特级初榨橄榄油和12种香醋——你可以用它们自制大量沙拉酱，以防那175种

cues.en: the store has on offer suits you.
cues.zh: 超市提供的沙拉酱都不合你意。

cues.en: So this is what the supermarket is like. And then you go to the consumer electronics store to set up a stereo system, speakers, CD player, tape player, tuner, amplifier.
cues.zh: 这就是超市的情况。然后你去消费电子商店配置一套音响系统，音箱、CD播放器、磁带播放器、调谐器、功放。

cues.en: And in this one
cues.zh: 而在这

cues.en: single consumer electronics store, there are that many stereo systems.
cues.zh: 一家消费电子商店里，就有那么多套音响系统。

cues.en: We can construct
cues.zh: 我们可以组合出

cues.en: six and a half million
cues.zh: 六百五十万

cues.en: different stereo systems out of the components that are on offer in one store. You gotta admit that's a lot of choice.
cues.zh: 套不同的音响系统，全都来自一家商店里提供的组件。你得承认，这选择可真是太多了。

cues.en: In other domains,
cues.zh: 在其他领域，

cues.en: the world of, communications.
cues.zh: 通信领域。

cues.en: There was a time when I was a boy when you could get any kind of telephone service you wanted as long as it came from Ma Bell.
cues.zh: 我小时候有段时间，你想要什么样的电话服务都行，只要它来自Ma Bell。

cues.en: You rented your phone, you didn't buy it. One consequence of that, by the way, is that the phone never broke. And,
cues.zh: 电话是租的，不是买的。顺便说一句，这么做的一个结果是电话从来不会坏。而且，

cues.en: those days are gone. We now have an almost unlimited variety of phones, especially in the world of cell phones.
cues.zh: 那些日子已经过去了。现在我们有了几乎无限种类的电话，尤其是在手机领域。

cues.en: These are cell phones of the future.
cues.zh: 这些是未来的手机。

cues.en: My favorite is the middle one, the m p three player nose hair trimmer and creme brulee torch. And if
cues.zh: 我最喜欢中间那个，MP3播放器鼻毛修剪器加焦糖布丁喷枪。而且如果

cues.en: if by some chance you haven't seen that in your store yet, you can rest assured that one day soon you will. And what this does is it leads people to walk into their stores asking this question.
cues.zh: 如果你碰巧还没在店里见过，放心，很快你就会见到的。而这带来的结果是，人们走进商店时会问这个问题。

cues.en: And do you know what the answer to this question now is? The answer is no.
cues.zh: 你知道现在这个问题的答案是什么吗？答案是不。

cues.en: It is not possible to buy a cell phone that doesn't do too much. So
cues.zh: 你买不到一部功能不过多的手机。所以

cues.en: in other aspects of life that are much more significant than, buying things, the same,
cues.zh: 在比买东西重要得多的生活的其他方面，同样的，

cues.en: explosion of choice is true. Health care.
cues.zh: 选择的爆炸也是真的。医疗。

cues.en: It is no longer the case in The United States that you
cues.zh: 在美国，已经不再是

cues.en: go to the doctor and the doctor tells you what to do. Instead, you go to the doctor and the doctor tells you, well, we could do a or we could do b. A has these benefits and these risks. B has these benefits and these risks.
cues.zh: 你去看医生，医生告诉你该怎么做。相反，你去看病，医生会告诉你：我们可以选 A 方案，也可以选 B 方案。A 有这些好处和风险，B 也有这些好处和风险。

cues.en: What do you want to do?
cues.zh: 你想怎么选？

cues.en: And you say, doc, what should I do? And the doc says, a has these benefits and risks, and b has these benefits of risks, what do you want to do?
cues.zh: 然后你说：“医生，我该怎么办？”医生却说：“A 有这些好处和风险，B 也有这些好处和风险，你想怎么选？”

cues.en: And you say,
cues.zh: 你接着问：

cues.en: if you were me, doc, what would you do? And the doc says, but I'm not you.
cues.zh: “医生，要是换作你，你会怎么选？”医生却说：“但我不是你啊。”

cues.en: And the result is, we call it patient autonomy,
cues.zh: 结果就是，我们把它称作“患者自主权”，

cues.en: which makes it sound like a good thing, but what it really is is a shifting of the burden and the responsibility for decision making from somebody who knows something, namely the doctor, somebody who knows nothing and is almost certainly sick and thus not in the best shape to be making decisions, namely the patient.
cues.zh: 听起来像是件好事，但实际上，它是把决策的负担和责任，从懂行的人（也就是医生）身上，甩给了一个对此一无所知、而且肯定还在生病因而不在最佳状态去作决定的人——也就是患者。

cues.en: There's enormous marketing of prescription drugs to people like you and me, which, if you think about it, makes no sense at all since we can't buy them. Why do they market to us if we can't buy them? The answer is that they expect us to call our doctors the next morning and ask for our prescriptions to be changed.
cues.zh: 现在有大量针对像你我这样的普通人的处方药广告营销；仔细想想这根本不合逻辑，因为我们自己根本买不了。既然买不了，为什么还要向我们推销？答案是，他们指望我们第二天一早给医生打电话，要求换处方。

cues.en: Something as dramatic
cues.zh: 甚至连像

cues.en: as our identity
cues.zh: 个人身份这样重大的事情，

cues.en: has now become a matter of choice,
cues.zh: 如今也变成了一种选择，

cues.en: as this slide is meant to, indicate.
cues.zh: 正如这张幻灯片所要展示的那样。

cues.en: We get to... We don't inherit an identity, we get to invent it, and we get to reinvent ourselves as often as we like. That means that every day when you wake up in the morning, you have to decide what kind of person
cues.zh: 我们可以……我们并非继承一种身份，而是可以自行创造，而且可以随心所欲地不断重塑自我。这意味着每天早晨醒来，你都得决定自己想成为什么样的人。

cues.en: you want to be.
cues.zh: 你想成为什么样的人。

cues.en: With respect to marriage and family,
cues.zh: 说到婚姻和家庭，

cues.en: there was a time when the default assumption
cues.zh: 曾经有一段时期，默认的假设是

cues.en: that almost everyone had is that you got married as soon as you could, and then you started having kids as soon as you could.
cues.zh: 几乎所有人都认为，能结婚就尽早结婚，然后能生孩子就尽早生孩子。

cues.en: The only real choice was who,
cues.zh: 唯一真正的选择是和谁结婚，

cues.en: not when and not what you did after.
cues.zh: 而不是何时结婚，也不是婚后做什么。

cues.en: Nowadays,
cues.zh: 如今，

cues.en: everything is very much up for grabs. I teach wonderfully intelligent students,
cues.zh: 一切都充满变数。我教的学生非常聪明，

cues.en: and, I assign 20% less work than I used to. And it's not because they're less smart, and it's not because they're less diligent.
cues.zh: 而且我布置的作业比过去少了20%。这不是因为他们变笨了，也不是因为他们不够勤奋。

cues.en: It's because they are preoccupied,
cues.zh: 而是因为他们心事重重，

cues.en: asking themselves,
cues.zh: 不断问自己：

cues.en: should I get married or not? Should I get married now? Should I get married later? Should I have kids first or a career first? All of these are consuming
cues.zh: 我该不该结婚？是现在结还是以后结？是先要孩子还是先拼事业？这些都是耗费心神的问题。

cues.en: questions. And they're gonna answer these questions whether or not it means not doing all the work I assign and not getting a good grade in my courses. And indeed, they should. These are important questions to answer.
cues.zh: 而且无论是否意味着完不成我布置的作业、拿不到好成绩，他们都会去回答这些问题。他们确实应该如此。这些都是必须回答的重要问题。

cues.en: Work.
cues.zh: 工作。

cues.en: We are blessed, as Carl was pointing out, with the technology that enables us to work
cues.zh: 正如卡尔所指出的，我们有幸拥有这样的技术，让我们能够工作

cues.en: every minute of every day from any place on the planet,
cues.zh: 在地球上任何地方，每一天的每一分钟都能工作，

cues.en: except the Randolph Hotel.
cues.zh: 除了兰道夫酒店。

cues.en: There is one corner,
cues.zh: 有一个角落，

cues.en: by the way, that I'm not going to tell anybody about where you... Actually, the where the high... Wi Fi works. I'm not telling you about it because I want to use it.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我不会告诉任何人的，就是那里……其实，就是那个Wi-Fi信号强的地方。我不告诉你们，是因为我想自己用。

cues.en: So what this means, this incredible freedom of choice we have with respect to work, is that we have to make a decision again and again and again about whether we should or shouldn't be working. We can go to watch our kid play soccer,
cues.zh: 所以这意味着，我们在工作方面拥有这种令人难以置信的选择自由，我们必须一次又一次地决定是否应该工作。我们可以去看孩子踢足球，

cues.en: and we have our cell phone on one hip and our BlackBerry on our other hip, and our laptop,
cues.zh: 一边口袋里装着手机，另一边装着BlackBerry，还有笔记本电脑，

cues.en: presumably, on our laps, and even if they're all shut off,
cues.zh: 大概就放在我们腿上，即使它们全都关着，

cues.en: every minute that we're watching our kid mutilate a soccer game, we are also asking ourselves, should I answer this cell phone call? Should I respond to this email? Should I draft this letter? And even if the answer to the question is no,
cues.zh: 我们看着孩子把足球赛踢得一团糟的每一分钟，我们也在问自己：我该接这个电话吗？我该回这封邮件吗？我该起草这封信吗？即使答案是“不”，

cues.en: it's certainly going to make the experience of your kid's soccer game very different than it would have been.
cues.zh: 这肯定会让你看孩子踢球的体验和原本截然不同。

cues.en: So everywhere we look,
cues.zh: 所以我们放眼望去，

cues.en: big things and small things, material things and lifestyle things, life is a matter of choice.
cues.zh: 大事小事，物质层面的、生活方式层面的，生活就是关于选择。

cues.en: And the world we used to live in looked like this.
cues.zh: 我们过去生活的世界是这样的。

cues.en: That is to say, there were some choices, but not everything was a matter of choice. And the world we now live in looks like this.
cues.zh: 也就是说，有一些选择，但并非一切都是选择。而我们现在生活的世界是这样的。

cues.en: And the question is,
cues.zh: 问题是，

cues.en: is this good news or bad news?
cues.zh: 这是好消息还是坏消息？

cues.en: And the answer
cues.zh: 答案是

cues.en: is yes.
cues.zh: 都是。

cues.en: We all know what's good about it, so I'm going to talk about what's bad about it.
cues.zh: 我们都知道它好在哪，所以我要讲讲它坏在哪。

cues.en: All of this choice has two effects,
cues.zh: 所有这些选择有两个影响，

cues.en: two negative effects on people.
cues.zh: 对人有两种负面影响。

cues.en: One effect,
cues.zh: 一个效果，

cues.en: paradoxically,
cues.zh: 矛盾的是，

cues.en: is that it produces paralysis
cues.zh: 它带来的就是瘫痪

cues.en: rather than liberation.
cues.zh: 而不是解放。

cues.en: With so many options to choose from, people find it very difficult to choose at all.
cues.zh: 可供选择的选项太多，反而让人很难做出选择。

cues.en: I'll give you one very dramatic example of this, a study that was done of investments
cues.zh: 我给大家举一个非常戏剧性的例子，这是一项关于投资的研究

cues.en: in voluntary
cues.zh: 在自愿的情况下

cues.en: retirement plans.
cues.zh: 退休计划。

cues.en: A colleague of mine got access to
cues.zh: 我的一位同事获得了访问权限，

cues.en: investment records from Vanguard,
cues.zh: 来自Vanguard的投资记录，

cues.en: the gigantic mutual fund company of about a million employees and about 2,000 different workplaces. And what she found is that for every 10 mutual funds the employer offered,
cues.zh: 一家拥有约百万员工、约2000个不同工作场所的巨型共同基金公司。她发现，雇主每提供10只共同基金，

cues.en: rate of participation
cues.zh: 参与率

cues.en: went down 2%.
cues.zh: 下降了 2%。

cues.en: You offer 50 funds, 10% fewer employees participate
cues.zh: 你们提供 50 只基金，参与员工少了 10%

cues.en: than if you only offer five.
cues.zh: 比你只提供五个要好。

cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 为什么？

cues.en: Because with 50 funds to choose from, it's so damn hard to decide which fund to choose that you'll just put it off till tomorrow, and then tomorrow and then tomorrow, and tomorrow, and and of course, tomorrow never comes. Understand
cues.zh: 因为要从50只基金里做选择，实在太难决定选哪只，所以你干脆拖到明天，再拖到明天、明天、明天，当然，明天永远不会到来。明白吗？

cues.en: that not only does this mean that people are going to have to eat dog food when they retire because they don't have enough money put away, it also means that making the decision is so hard that they pass up significant matching money from the employer. By not participating,
cues.zh: 这不仅意味着人们退休后钱不够，只能省吃俭用，还意味着做这个决定太难，以至于他们放弃了雇主提供的大笔匹配资金。因为不参与，

cues.en: they are passing up as much as $5,000
cues.zh: 他们放弃的金额高达5000美元

cues.en: a year from the employer who would happily match their contribution.
cues.zh: 一年后，雇主会乐意匹配他们的缴款。

cues.en: So paralysis
cues.zh: 所以，瘫痪

cues.en: is a consequence of having too many choices, and I think it makes the world look like this.
cues.zh: 是选择过多的一种后果，我觉得这会让世界看起来像这样。

cues.en: You
cues.zh: 你

cues.en: really want to get the decision right if it's for all eternity. Right? You don't want to pick the wrong mutual fund or even the wrong salad dresser. So that's one effect. The second effect is that even if we manage to overcome the paralysis and make a choice,
cues.zh: 如果这是为了永恒，你真的想把决定做对。对吧？你不想选错共同基金，甚至选错沙拉酱。所以这是第一个影响。第二个影响是，即使我们设法克服了瘫痪并做出了选择，

cues.en: we end up less satisfied
cues.zh: 我们最终对选择的结果

cues.en: with the result of the choice than we would be if we had fewer options to choose from.
cues.zh: 还不如选项较少时那么满意。

cues.en: And there are several reasons for this.
cues.zh: 这有几个原因。

cues.en: One of them is that with a lot of different salad dressings to choose from, if you buy one and it's not perfect, and you know what salad dressing is, it's easy to imagine that you could have made a different choice that would have been better.
cues.zh: 其中之一是，面对许多不同的沙拉酱可选，如果你买了一种但不完美，而你知道沙拉酱是什么样，就很容易想象你本可以做出更好的不同选择。

cues.en: And what happens is this imagined
cues.zh: 随之而来的是，这种想象的

cues.en: alternative
cues.zh: 替代选项

cues.en: induces you to regret the decision you made, and this regret subtracts from the satisfaction you get out of the decision you made, even if it was a good decision.
cues.zh: 会让你对所做的决定感到后悔，而这种后悔会削弱你从决定中获得的满足感，即使那是个好决定。

cues.en: The more options there are, the easier it is to regret anything at all that is disappointing about the option that you chose.
cues.zh: 选项越多，就越容易对你所选选项中任何令人失望之处感到后悔。

cues.en: Second, what economists call opportunity costs. Dan Gilbert made a big point this morning of talking about how
cues.zh: 其次，是经济学家所说的机会成本。Dan Gilbert今天早上重点谈到了

cues.en: how much, the the way in which we value things depends on what we compare them to.
cues.zh: 我们看待事物的价值有多少、在多大程度上取决于我们拿它们与什么相比。

cues.en: Well, when there are lots of alternatives to consider,
cues.zh: 当有许多替代方案需要考虑时，

cues.en: it is easy to imagine the attractive features of alternatives that you reject,
cues.zh: 就很容易想象你所拒绝的替代方案的吸引人之处，

cues.en: that make you less satisfied with the alternative that you've chosen. Here's an example.
cues.zh: 这让你对已选择的方案不那么满意。这里有个例子。

cues.en: For those of you who aren't New Yorkers, I apologize.
cues.zh: 对于那些不是纽约人的朋友，我表示歉意。

cues.en: But here's what you're supposed to be thinking. Here's this couple on the Hamptons,
cues.zh: 但你应该这样想。这对夫妇在汉普顿，

cues.en: very expensive real estate, gorgeous beach, beautiful day. They have it all to themselves. What could be better? Well, damn it, this guy is thinking, it's August.
cues.zh: 非常昂贵的房产，美丽的海滩，美好的天气。他们独享这一切。还有什么比这更好的呢？嗯，见鬼，这家伙在想，现在是八月。

cues.en: Everybody in my Manhattan neighborhood is away.
cues.zh: 我曼哈顿社区的人都外出了。

cues.en: I could be parking right in front of my building.
cues.zh: 我本可以把车直接停在我家楼前。

cues.en: And he spends two weeks nagged
cues.zh: 而他花了两周时间被困扰着

cues.en: by the idea that he is missing the opportunity day after day to have a great parking space.
cues.zh: 日复一日地想着自己错过了获得绝佳停车位的机会。

cues.en: Opportunity costs subtract from the satisfaction we get out of what we choose, even when what we choose is terrific.
cues.zh: 机会成本会削减我们从所选择事物中获得的满足感，即使我们所选择的事物非常棒。

cues.en: And the more options there are to consider, the more attractive features of these options are going to be reflected by us as opportunity costs.
cues.zh: 可供考虑的选择越多，这些选项中吸引人的特点就越会被我们视为机会成本。

cues.en: Here's another example.
cues.zh: 再举一个例子。

cues.en: Now now this cartoon makes a lot of points. It makes points about living in the moment as well, and probably about doing things slowly. But one point it makes is that whenever you're choosing one thing, you're choosing not to do other things, and those other things may have lots of attractive features, and it's going to make what you're doing less attractive.
cues.zh: 现在，这幅漫画说明了很多问题。它也指出了活在当下的重要性，可能还关于慢慢做事。但它说明的一点是，每当你选择一件事时，你就是在选择不做其他事情，而那些其他事情可能有很多吸引人的特点，这会让你正在做的事情显得不那么有吸引力。

cues.en: Third,
cues.zh: 第三，

cues.en: escalation of expectations.
cues.zh: 期望的升级。

cues.en: This hit me when I went to replace my jeans. I wear jeans almost all the time, and there was a time when jeans came in one flavor, and you bought them, and they fit like crap, and they were incredibly uncomfortable. And if you wore them long enough and washed them enough times, they started to fit... Feel okay.
cues.zh: 当我想要换牛仔裤时，这一点让我深有感触。我几乎一直穿牛仔裤，曾经有一段时间，牛仔裤只有一种款式，你买了它，它穿起来很糟糕，极其不舒服。但如果你穿得足够久，洗得足够多次，它们就开始合身了……感觉还行。

cues.en: So I went to replace my jeans after years and years of wearing these old ones, and I said, I want a pair of jeans, here's my size. And the shopkeeper said, do you want slim fit, easy fit, relaxed fit? Do want button fly or zipper fly? Do want stonewashed or acid washed? Do you want them distressed? Do you want bootcut? Do you want tapered? Blah blah blah. On and on. He went, my jaw dropped.
cues.zh: 所以我穿了多年旧牛仔裤后，决定去换条新的。我说，我要一条牛仔裤，这是我的尺码。店主问，你要修身版、舒适版、宽松版？要纽扣门襟还是拉链门襟？要石洗还是酸洗？要不要做旧？要靴型裤还是锥形裤？等等等等。他说个没完，我目瞪口呆。

cues.en: And after I recovered, I said, I want the kind that used to be the only kind.
cues.zh: 等我缓过神来，我说，我想要以前唯一那种款式。

cues.en: He had no idea what that was.
cues.zh: 他完全不知道那是什么。

cues.en: So I spent an hour trying on all these damn jeans, and I walked out of the store, truth, with the best fitting jeans I had ever had. I did better. All this choice made it possible for me to do better.
cues.zh: 于是我花了一个小时试穿所有这些该死的牛仔裤，然后走出店门——说实话——我买到了有史以来最合身的牛仔裤。我确实选得更好了。所有这些选择让我能选得更好。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: I felt worse.
cues.zh: 我感觉更糟了。

cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 为什么？

cues.en: I wrote a whole book to try to explain this to myself. The reason is
cues.zh: 我写了整整一本书，想向自己解释这件事。原因是

cues.zh: 我感觉更糟的原因是，有这么多的选项，

cues.zh: 我的期望

cues.zh: 对一条牛仔裤应该有多好的期望，被抬高了。

cues.en: I had very low ex... I had no particular expectations when they only came in one flavor. When they came in a 100 flavors, damn it, one of them should have been perfect.
cues.zh: 我原本期望很低……当只有一种款式时，我没什么特别的期望。可当有100种款式时，该死，总该有一种是完美的吧。

cues.en: And what I got was good, but it wasn't perfect. And so I compared what I got to what I expected,
cues.zh: 而我得到的虽然不错，但并不完美。于是我把得到的和期望的做了比较，

cues.en: what and I got was disappointing in comparison to what I expected.
cues.zh: 结果就是，跟我的期望相比，我得到的让人失望。

cues.en: Adding options to people's lives can't help but increase the expectations people have about how good those options will be. And what that's going to produce is less satisfaction with with results even when they're good results.
cues.zh: 给人们的生活增加选项，只会抬高人们对这些选项能有多好的期望。而这带来的结果，就是对结果更不满意——哪怕结果已经很好。

cues.en: Nobody in the world of marketing knows this.
cues.zh: 营销界没人懂这个道理。

cues.en: Because if they did,
cues.zh: 因为如果他们懂，

cues.en: you wouldn't all know what this was about.
cues.zh: 你们就不会都知道这是怎么回事了。

cues.en: The truth is more like this.
cues.zh: 真相其实更像是这样。

cues.en: The reason that everything was better back when everything was worse is that when everything was worse, it was actually possible for people to have experiences that were a pleasant surprise.
cues.zh: 一切更糟的时候反而一切更好的原因在于，当一切更糟时，人们实际上还有可能获得令人愉快的惊喜体验。

cues.zh: 幸福的秘诀就是

cues.zh: 我想说

cues.zh: 一点自传式的

cues.zh: 小插曲，

cues.zh: 我确实娶了位妻子，她非常棒。我不可能找到更好的了。我没有将就。

cues.zh: 但将就也不总是坏事。最后，

cues.en: of buying a bad fitting pair of jeans when there is only one kind to buy is that when you are dissatisfied and you ask why, who's responsible?
cues.zh: 就是当你只有一种牛仔裤可买，却买了条不合身的，你不满意，问这是谁的责任？

cues.zh: 答案很清楚。是世界的问题。你能怎么办？

cues.en: When there are hundreds of different styles of genes available,
cues.zh: 当有几百种不同款式的牛仔裤可选，

cues.zh: 而你买了一条令人失望的，

cues.zh: 你问为什么，谁的责任？

cues.en: It is equally clear that the answer to the question is you.
cues.zh: 同样清楚的是，答案就是你自己。

cues.en: You could have done better. With a thousand... With a 100 different kinds of genes on display, there is no excuse for failure. And so when people make decisions,
cues.zh: 你本可以做得更好。有一千……有一百种不同的基因展示出来，就没有失败的借口。所以当人们做决定时，

cues.zh: 即使决定的结果是好的，他们也会感到失望

cues.zh: 临床抑郁症在工业世界上一代人中爆发式增长。

cues.zh: 我相信一个重要因素，不是唯一因素，但是一个重要因素，

cues.zh: 导致了抑郁症和自杀的激增，

cues.zh: 是因为人们有失望的经历，因为他们的标准太高了，然后当他们必须向自己解释这些经历时，他们认为自己有错。

cues.zh: 让我提醒你们，这是官方教条，

cues.en: the one that we all take to be true,
cues.zh: 我们都认为是正确的那个，

cues.en: and it's all false.
cues.zh: 而它全是假的。

cues.zh: 它不是真的。

cues.en: There's no question that some choice is better than none,
cues.zh: 毫无疑问，有些选择比没有好，

cues.en: but it doesn't follow from that that more choice is better than some choice. There's some magical amount. I don't know what it is. I'm pretty confident that we have long since passed the point where options improve our welfare.
cues.zh: 但这并不意味着更多选择就比一些选择好。有一个神奇的量。我不知道是什么。我相当确信我们早已过了选项能改善我们福祉的那个点。

cues.zh: 现在，作为一个政策问题……我快说完了。
